RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, November 9, 2010/Kartika 18, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Panchayati Raj; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Rural Development; Shipping)
Total number of questions — 20
Outsourcing of airport services by
NACIL
*1. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL: Will
the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Aviation
Company of India Limited (NACIL) has
outsourced various services at the Mumbai
and Delhi airports;
(b) if so, the details of the services
outsourced along with the procedures
specified for the purpose;
(c) whether complaints have been
received regarding irregularities in the
engagement of the outsourced agencies by
NACIL; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
follow-up action taken thereon?
Guidelines on Corporate Social
Responsibility
*2. SHRI R.C. SINGH:  Will the Minister
of HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of guidelines issued by
the Department of Public Sector
Enterprises on Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR);
(b) whether the guidelines are applicable
to private corporate sector along with the
Central Public Sector Undertakings
(CPSUs); and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Reunitization of contribution to NPS
*3. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE  be pleased to refer
to answer to Unstarred Question 2471
given in the Rajya Sabha on 17 August,
2010 and state:
(a) whether New Pension Scheme
(NPS) contributions received upto 31
March, 2010 have been allocated
@ NAV of `one per unit;
(b) if so, the reasons for showing NA V
@ `1 per unit pending reunitization in the
statement of transactions of NPS
beneficiaries;
(c) the meaning of pending reunitization
once it has been allocated @ `1;
(d) the reasons for keeping unitization
pending for more than six years since
January, 2004; and

2
(e) whether lack of such transparency
may lead to a big scam of hard earned
money of NPS beneficiaries?
MGNREGS in Goa
 *4. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK:  Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) since when the Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme (MGNREGS) is being
implemented in Goa;
(b)  the rate of wages paid to the workers
at the time of the commencement of the
Scheme and at present;
(c)  the total amount of wages paid, so
far, taluka-wise and district-wise; and
(d) the details regarding the procedure
adopted by Government for monitoring the
Scheme?
Extension of credits to agriculture and
micro-small and medium industrial
sectors
*5. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) the allocations for Agriculture and
Micro-Small-Medium Industries credits
through Public Sector Banks during 2007
and 2008;
(b) whether these allocations were fully
utilized; and
(c) the recovery status during 2007 and
2008 and its percentage thereof viz-a-viz
loans sanctioned?
Innovative treatment models to
combat threat from cancer
*6. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether researchers from across the
world in a public health policy paper have
stressed the need for a large scale response
to combat the threat from cancer;
(b) if so, whether the researchers have
also stressed the need to employ innovative
treatment models and new investment
options to control cancer;
(c) whether the deaths occuring due to
cancer in India are increasing and even the
cost of treatment is very high; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to fight such a dangerous disease?
Coverage  under NPS
*7. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of FINANCE  be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that various
nationalized and private banks are unwilling
to sell National Pension System (NPS) to
poor persons;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed
to be taken to increase the coverage under
NPS?
Mandatory labelling of GM foods
*8. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any provision to
ensure mandatory labelling of Genetically
Modified (GM) Foods;
(b) if so, whether there is any proper
mechanism to ensure the implementation
of labelling; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

3
Losses due to DTAA with Mauritius
†*9. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
FINANCE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is incurring a loss of about `2000 crores
annually on account of Double Taxation
Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) executed
with Mauritius;
(b) if so, by  when steps would be taken
by Government to check this; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Investigation report on Mangalore
plane crash
†*10. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the investigation report
regarding Air India plane crash near
Mangalore on 22 May, 2010, in which 158
passengers were killed, has been received;
(b) whether the main reason behind the
crash was the pilot having gone to sleep
under the influence of alcohol and taking
a wrong direction;
(c) the steps being taken to prevent such
accidents in future; and
(d) in view of addiction of alcohol noticed
in most of the pilots, whether they are
examined before the take off of the flight?
Pictorial warnings on tobacco products
*11. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether stronger pictorial warnings
on tobacco products are deterrent to
tobacco use;
(b) whether as per some studies, the
existing pictorial health warnings on
tobacco products are inadequate in
conveying the adverse impact of tobacco
on health;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) what are the technical issues
involved in implementation of new
pictorial warnings?
Allocation of natural gas to non-core
sector
*12. SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN
SINGH: Will th e Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some
unscrupulous private companies are
manipulating to obtain natural gas for their
non-core industries;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether by allocating natural gas/
fuel to non-core industries, non-core sector
customers get themselves enriched at the
expense of Government revenue;
(d) if so, the action taken or proposed
to be taken against erring officials who are
responsible for allocation of natural gas to
non-core sector; and
(e) the names of non-core sector
companies which have been allotted natural
gas during the last one year with details of
quantity etc.?
Deaths due to Japanese Encephalitis
†*13. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
immunization against Japanese
Encephalitis could not be taken up this year
because its vaccine got spoilt during its
storage as a result of which the disease
spread widely leading to increased fatality
among children;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

4
(b) the number of deaths due to this
disease and the age group of the people
afflicted with this disease, State-wise
during the last three years; and
(c) the facilities provided by the Central
Government during the last three years to
affected States to tackle this disease?
Recovery of outstanding dues  of
various airlines by AAI
*14. SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether many scheduled airlines and
foreign carriers owe  huge amount of
money to the Airports Authority of India
(AAI);
(b) if so, the details of outstanding dues
of various airlines as on 31 October, 2010,
airline-wise;
(c) the steps taken by the AAI to recover
such pending security deposits from
various airlines, so far;
(d) the details of the practices followed
internationally in this regard;
(e) whether various airlines registered
in the country have to deposit such similar
charges to various airports at the end of
October, 2010; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Selection of implementing agencies
under NRLM
*15. DR. T.N. SEEMA: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) the criteria for selection of
implementing agencies under the National
Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM);
(b) the role of the Local Self
Government Institutions in the selection
and implementation of schemes under
NRLM; and
(c) whether the Central Government
intends to award contracts for
implementation of the schemes under
NRLM and transfer funds to the
implementing agencies directly, by passing
the State Governments?
Gas supply from Turkmenistan
*16. SHRI H.K. DUA: Will the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has signed a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for
transporting gas from Turkmenistan
through Afghanistan and Pakistan;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when gas will start reaching
India, and at what cost?
Increase in enrolment by medical
colleges
†*17. SHRI NARESH CHANDRA
AGRAW AL: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is
contemplating to double the number of
enrolments for seeking admission in
existing Government and private medical
colleges in the country keeping in view the
paucity of doctors in urban  and rural areas;
(b) if so, the criteria fixed therefor and
by when the decision would be taken in
this regard; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

5
Purchase of new ships by SCI
*18. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:  Will
the Minister of SHIPPING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Shipping
Corporation of India (SCI) intends to
purchase new ships to enhance its capacity-
utilisation;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether plans have been chalked-
out about the manner in which these ships
would be used in future; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Recapitalization of Urban Co-
Operative Banks
†*19. SHRI PARSHOTTAM
KHODABHAI RUPALA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry is aware that
the financial condition of Urban Co-
operative Banks in the country is
deteriorating day by day and financially
sound Urban Co-operative Banks are not
taking much interest in taking over the
business of financially weaker Urban Co-
operative Banks;
(b) whether the account holders and
stakeholders of the financially weaker
Urban Co-operative Banks are not showing
much willingness to convert more than one
lakh rupees of their deposited amount into
shares as a result of which RBI's recent
scheme of recapitalization of financially
weaker Urban Co-operative Banks could
not materialize; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Taxation cases pending for
adjudication
*20. PROF. ANIL KUMAR SAHANI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of cases lying pending
for adjudication with departmental officers
in Central Excise, Customs  and Service
Tax, as on date;
(b) the number of cases lying pending
with them for more than over one year, two
years and more than three years;
(c) the quantum of money locked in
these cases;
(d) whether there is any time limit for
the disposal of such cases;
(e) if so, the reasons for not adhering to
the said time limit; and
(f) whether there is any proposal to
initiate departmental proceedings against
these officers for not disposing off the cases
within the time limit?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 3rd November, 2010 Secretary-General.
Kartika 12, 1932 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 1, 10, 14,
Finance : 3, 5, 7, 9, 19, 20,
Health and Family Welfare : 6, 8, 11, 13, 17,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises :2 ,
Panchayati Raj :—
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 12, 16,
Rural Development : 4, 15,
Shipping : 18.
GMGIPMRND—4919RS(S-3)—03.11.2010.
